Package io.github.jspinak.brobot.runner.json.parsing.exception

Class ConfigurationException

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Throwable
java.lang.Exception
io.github.jspinak.brobot.runner.json.parsing.exception.ConfigurationException
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ConfigurationException extends Exception
Exception thrown when configuration processing fails in the Brobot framework.

This exception represents various configuration-related failures including:

  • JSON parsing errors - Malformed JSON syntax
  • Schema validation failures - JSON doesn't conform to expected schema
  • Missing required fields - Required configuration elements are absent
  • Type mismatches - Values have incorrect types
  • File I/O errors - Configuration files cannot be read/written
  • Path navigation errors - Invalid JSON paths or missing nodes

The exception can optionally carry a ValidationResult containing detailed validation errors when the failure is due to schema validation. This allows for comprehensive error reporting with specific field-level issues.

Common usage patterns:

  • Simple error: new ConfigurationException("Config file not found")
  • With cause: new ConfigurationException("Parse failed", ioException)
  • With validation: new ConfigurationException("Invalid config", validationResult)
  • Formatted: ConfigurationException.formatted("Missing field: %s", fieldName)

    • ConfigurationException

      public ConfigurationException(String message)
      Creates a configuration exception with an error message.

      Use this constructor for simple error cases where no underlying cause or validation details are available.

      Parameters:
      message - The error message describing what went wrong

    • ConfigurationException

      public ConfigurationException(String message, Throwable cause)
      Creates a configuration exception with an error message and underlying cause.

      Use this constructor when the configuration error is caused by another exception, such as IOException during file reading or JsonProcessingException during parsing.

      Parameters:
      message - The error message describing what went wrong
      cause - The underlying exception that caused this configuration error

    • ConfigurationException

      public ConfigurationException(String message, ValidationResult validationResult)
      Creates a configuration exception with validation details.

      Use this constructor when the error is due to schema validation failure. The ValidationResult provides detailed information about which fields failed validation and why.

      Parameters:
      message - The high-level error message
      validationResult - Detailed validation errors (null-safe, creates empty result if null)

    • ConfigurationException

      public ConfigurationException(String message, Throwable cause, ValidationResult validationResult)
      Creates a configuration exception with full error context.

      Use this constructor when you have both an underlying cause and validation details. This provides the most comprehensive error information for debugging.

      Parameters:
      message - The high-level error message
      cause - The underlying exception that triggered the validation
      validationResult - Detailed validation errors (null-safe, creates empty result if null)

  • Method Details

    • formatted

      public static ConfigurationException formatted(String format, Object... args)
      Creates a configuration exception with a formatted message.

      This factory method provides a convenient way to create exceptions with parameterized messages using String.format() syntax. It helps avoid string concatenation and makes messages more readable.

      Example: 

      
 throw ConfigurationException.formatted(
     "Invalid value '%s' for field '%s'", value, fieldName);
      Parameters:
      format - The format string (as per String.format())
      args - The arguments to be formatted into the message
      Returns:
      A new ConfigurationException with the formatted message
